agent_notes: Lamech's naming speech at 5:29 ('this one will comfort us') is a hope about Noah, not an oracle. A later chapter (Gen 8-9) may link it; no FULFILLS_PROPHECY is written here, since it is neither God's nor a prophet's word.

Gen 5:32 says Noah was 500 when he began to father Shem, Ham and Japheth; the three need not be born in one year. Gen 11:10 (Shem was 100 two years after the Flood) puts Shem in Noah's 502nd year, so the offset 500 years with a margin of 3 years would also fit; I used 500 and a 3-year margin to cover this. Rashi and Radak on 5:32 give reasons for the late age; I do not follow them.

notes.note: Gen 5 is the dated genealogy, so it is the chronology itself: one birth event per father-to-son step (offset = the father's age at begetting, from the father's own birth START) and one death event per patriarch (offset = the age at death, from his own birth). The chain starts on anchor.creation through Adam and agrees with the anchor's basis: 130+105+90+70+65+162+65+187+182 = 1056 years from creation to Noah's birth.

Verses 5:1-2 (the heading, 'in the day God created man') are a recap of Gen 1:26-28, not a new event; they are covered by the parent evt.gen_5.adam_genealogy, which spans 5:1-32. Every other verse is in a birth or death event.

No causal links are written. A genealogy shows sequence, which the timeline already holds, and the text states no cause apart from Lamech's naming hope, which is dropped for the reason above. There is no divine or prophetic speech in the chapter to check for fulfilment.

Ages are the Masoretic numbers, as the anchors are. The LXX and Samaritan numbers in Gen 5 differ (for example the LXX has Adam begetting Seth at 230), and are a different chronology, not covered by the margins.
